links.comparator_used: Symptom-only screening algorithms (cough ≥2 weeks; any symptom) for deciding who gets Xpert testing
links.outcome: Bacteriologically-confirmed TB cases detected, cost per case detected and ICER in active case finding
links.effect: Abnormality ≥0.30 OR any symptom detected 85 cases at US$773 per case (total US$65704). Cough ≥2 weeks detected 34 cases at US$1198 per case (US$40740). Any symptom detected 77 cases at US$636 per case (US$48939). Versus the cough ≥2 weeks baseline, the ICER was US$191 per additional case for any symptom and US$2096 for Abnormality ≥0.30 OR any symptom. CXR-AI-only algorithms (≥0.30: 81 cases, ≥0.50: 76 cases) were dominated. CXR-AI cost per case fell below any-symptom screening only when asymptomatic TB exceeded about 30% of cases.
links.tradeoff: Algorithms using CXR and AI had the highest total cost, driven by ultraportable X-ray and AI licence costs (US$75000 and US$9000) and Xpert cartridges. Cost per case was higher than any-symptom screening in the main analysis. Asymptomatic TB was only about 10% of cases in this population.
links.quote: Compared to traditional symptom screening, using CXR and AI or combination with symptoms detects more cases at lower cost per case detected.

design_hint: alert threshold selection (AI abnormality score cutoffs combined with symptom screening)
